title: Add quantization profile baseline selection (by model family + GPU SKU) for quality gates
author: Arjun Desai
description: Context: Quality gates for Optimize need a stable, apples-to-apples baseline when evaluating quantization profile changes. Today, gate runs pick a baseline based on “current deployed config” which can vary by region / hardware and sometimes points at a different GPU SKU than the target (esp. when capacity causes temporary spillover). That makes quantization deltas noisy and occasionally wrong. This PR introduces explicit baseline selection for quantization profile diffs based on (model_family, gpu_sku) with guardrails, logging, and tests. What this adds: (1) Baseline selection logic for quantization gating: new BaselineSelector that resolves a baseline config for gate runs using model family + canonical GPU SKU + runtime-compat constraints (context window bucket + kv_cache_mode). (2) Baseline source precedence: a) exact match: (model_family, gpu_sku) pinned “golden baseline” entry; b) compatible fallback: same model_family on sku_class (e.g., "ampere"), if explicitly marked allow_fallback=true; c) last-resort: fp16_default baseline for the model_family with gate marked degraded=true and enforcement requiring “full gates” (smoke tier cannot pass degraded baselines). (3) Guardrails: blocks baseline selection if it would cross architecture boundaries (e.g., hopper -> ampere) unless allow_fallback is set AND quant profile is marked "arch_compatible"; blocks if baseline model version differs from the gate baseline version requested by Optimize (prevents comparing different weights). (4) Persistence + auditability: gate_run record now stores baseline_profile_id, baseline_reason, and baseline_selector_version. (5) Metrics/logs: emits optimize.gates.baseline_selection.{success,failure} with tags (model_family, gpu_sku, reason, degraded). (6) Tests: unit tests for selection matrix + integration test that verifies the eval-harness request payload includes baseline_profile_id and that degraded baselines force full gates. Why this is safe: It only affects gate evaluation inputs for quantization config diffs (no runtime inference path change). If selector cannot find a safe baseline, we fail the gate run early with an explicit error (BaselineSelectionError) rather than running a misleading comparison. Related work: - ENG-3924 (this PR) - pr-19511 (config diff schema/validation) - pr-19523 (Optimize -> eval-harness wiring) - eval-harness pr-418 (flake score / rerun policy) Notes: This intentionally does not auto-create baseline entries. Baseline registry is seeded from existing “known-good” configs per model family + SKU (see migration + fixtures). Follow-up: add a small admin tool to list missing baselines per region/SKU during rollout (separate PR).
commits: optimize/gates: introduce BaselineSelector interface and quant baseline resolver
db: add baseline_profile registry + gate_run baseline metadata fields
runtime/sku: canonicalize GPU SKU mapping + sku_class helper
gates: enforce degraded baseline behavior (requires full gates)
tests: add selection matrix fixtures and integration coverage
obs: baseline selection metrics + structured logs
conversation: Grace Kim (review): Baseline selection looks right, but I’m worried about cross-arch fallbacks. Even if a profile is marked arch_compatible, are we still comparing kernels that can change numerics? Also, can we ensure we never compare H100 target against A100 baseline unless explicitly opted-in? Arjun Desai (author): Agree. I tightened the guardrail: default is “no cross-arch”, and the only allowed cross-arch path is when (a) baseline entry allow_fallback=true AND (b) the quant profile is explicitly marked arch_compatible AND (c) sku_class matches (e.g., hopper->hopper). I removed the earlier mapping that let hopper fall back to ampere. Added tests for this. Noah Patel (review): Please add a hard block if baseline model version differs from the requested baseline model version. We’ve had gate runs comparing different weight revisions due to canary weight rollouts. Arjun: Added model_version equality check and a clearer error message: BaselineSelectionError: WEIGHTS_MISMATCH. Also logging includes baseline_model_version + requested. Jonas Weber (review): For degraded baselines, I want to ensure we don’t accidentally allow smoke gates to pass and then promote based on weak evidence. Can we enforce “full gates required” when degraded=true? Arjun: Implemented: if degraded baseline is used, smoke tier is auto-failed with reason “DEGRADED_BASELINE_REQUIRES_FULL_GATES” and Optimize will need to run full gates. Added integration test that asserts gate tier behavior. Olivia Grant (review): Eval-harness expects baseline config details, not just an id, for reproducibility. Are we sending the selected baseline config payload deterministically? Arjun: We still send the baseline_config snapshot (existing behavior), but now we also include baseline_profile_id + selector_version + reason. Snapshot comes from the baseline_profiles registry so it’s stable. CI note: First run failed on integration tests due to fixture ordering in baseline_profiles.fixture.json; fixed by sorting and making selection deterministic. Mateo Alvarez (review): Looks good. Please add a quick note in internal docs about how to seed baseline profiles for new GPU SKUs. Arjun: Added docs/internal/quality-gates/baselines.md section “Adding a new SKU baseline” with examples and required fields. Approvals: Grace approved after guardrail tightening. Noah approved after WEIGHTS_MISMATCH block. Jonas approved after degraded-tier enforcement. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal: Quality gate runs for quantization profile changes now select a stable baseline per model family + GPU SKU and will fail fast on unsafe/ambiguous baseline comparisons. Degraded baselines require full gates (smoke tier cannot pass).
